kicker: Hotrod Outdoor Alaska Fishing · round report
title: Asset Quality Round
lede: 36 changes across every family of assets, from rounder animals and lit-through grass to clear car glass and a truer tone curve, each using what the game already draws. Measured against the previous build: the still world's draw calls 1605.0 → 1603.7, shader programs 105 → 102, no new texture memory (the renderer holds 111 textures before and 111 after), frame time +0.08 ms (no clear difference) and +0.04 ms at an iPhone's size (no clear difference). The audit found two visible faults and four extra shaders, all fixed.

sections.title: What this round set out to do
sections.html:
The request: "Increase the perceived graphic quality without increasing load on the system. Look through all the assets and increase quality. Then do an audit afterwards."

Load was read as everything a phone pays for: draw calls, triangles, the textures and their memory, the shader programs, the script's memory, the processor's side of every frame, the time to load, and the work each pixel's shader does. The first five are counted by the budget check, the frame and load times are timed in turns against the previous build, and the per-pixel work was read in the shaders, since the test machine draws in software and cannot time a phone's graphics chip.

RequestWhat was doneStatus
Look through all the assets and increase qualityEvery family of assets was gone through: the models built in code (animals, birds, fish, cars, boat, buildings, props, statues, the hands), the trees, shrubs and rocks, the textures, the ground, the water, the sky and light, and the final picture. 36 changes, listed below with what each costs.Done
Without increasing load on the systemDraw calls over the eight budget places 1930.0 before and 1929.7 after (0.0%); the still world without the animals 1605.0 and 1603.7; triangles 0.0%; textures held by the renderer 111 and 111 (the materials use 86 and 87: the race car's carbon now shares the scene's reflection map); shader programs 105 and 102; script memory 190 and 190 MB. Frame time, timed in turns: +0.08 ms at 320 by 180 and +0.04 ms at an iPhone's size. Time to load: −0.06 s.See Load and Frame time
Then do an audit afterwardsAn independent code review (12 findings, all fixed or reduced), every shader built on a development build at High, Medium and Low (254 programs, 0 failed), 27 regression scenarios (27 clean), and fifteen fixed views before and after.See Audit

sections.title: What changed, and what it costs
sections.html:
Every change uses what the game already draws: the same meshes, the same textures at the same sizes, the same shaders or cheaper ones. Where something costs a little, it says so. "Load time only" means work done once while the world is built.

AssetsWhat changedCost when playing
Every built model (animals, buildings, props, cars, boat, tools, statues)Round parts (cylinders, spheres and rings of six sides or more, cones of eight or more) keep smooth normals instead of being shaded facet by facet, so logs, posts, trunks, wheels and bodies read as round. Square posts and five-sided far trunks stay prisms.None: the same vertices, and every vertex stores a normal already.
Every built modelColour variation without diagonal splits: a flat part gets one tone per face, shared by the two triangles of a quad (before, each triangle had its own and every quad showed its diagonal); a smooth part gets a tone that varies smoothly across its surface.None: vertex colours were there already.
Wheels, hubcaps, fish bodies, the geyser cone and other turned shapesNormals averaged across the seam where a turned or lofted shape repeats its first column of vertices, and across points repeated round an axis: the light no longer creases along one line of every wheel and stars at its middle. Real edges (a rim, a lip) stay sharp.Load time only (worked out once while the world is built).
Moose, caribou, deer, wolf, fox, hare, lynx, black and grizzly bearsCountershading as on the real animals: a lighter belly blending in below the flank, a darker back, and a grizzled lighter back on the bears. The caribou's underside is pale instead of dark brown.None: vertex colours.
Gull, goose and duckPale wing undersides, seen whenever a bird flies over; the gull's black wingtips stay black.None: vertex colours.
Static models standing on the ground (buildings, fences, props, rocks set in the scenery)Darker where they meet the ground, fading out over 1.6 m, as soil and shade darken the foot of anything standing outdoors (baked ambient darkening): sides and undersides only, since a face turned up to the open sky (a deck, a table top, the top of a log) is not shaded by the ground. Glass and lamps, which have no vertex colours, are left alone.Load time only: worked out once on each model's vertex colours.
Spruce, birch, poplar and aspen crownsCrowns lit as one soft volume, as a crown of many small leaves is, instead of as a few big facets: a spruce faces out from its trunk and a little up, a leafy crown out from its centre. Every distance version of a tree gets the same normals, so a tree does not change its lighting when it is swapped for a nearer version.None: the same vertices with different normals.
SpruceThe low whorls sit in the shade of the ones above, the inside of each whorl is darker and the tips are fresh, lighter and a little yellower growth.None: vertex colours.
Birch, aspen and poplar trunksThe bark keeps its own grey and white under the per-tree tint, so an autumn or gold crown no longer turns its trunk yellow. Far off, where a trunk is a three-sided sliver, the trees keep the shared far-foliage shader.A few instructions in the vertex shader of the near trees only; no new shader, texture or draw.
Trunks, logs and snagsDarker where a trunk sits in the ground; logs and dead snags in weathered greys and browns.None: vertex colours and existing tints.
Rocks and bouldersStone that changes from area to area: cool grey greywacke, warm granite and rust-stained rock, and some stones lying as flat slabs (a boat now floats over a sunken slab as low as it really is).None: the per-instance tint and scale already existed.
Fish (caught, on the line and swimming)Closed snout and tail root (no hole), no crease along the belly, and the rainbow sheen of scales on salmon, trout, whitefish and grayling, with barely a trace on cod, rockfish, sharks and the rest. Fins are drawn with alpha to coverage on the multisampled frame instead of blending, so they never draw over a nearer fin.Less: both eyes in one mesh (one draw fewer per fish); the fins cast no shadow (alpha to coverage would have needed a shadow shader of its own).
Small fish in the waterThe tail fin's two sides on vertices of their own (with shared vertices the normals cancelled and the fin lit at random) and a paler belly.None.
Hot rodClear glass: the scene behind shows through dimmed a tenth with the sky reflected on top, instead of a milky blue film. Tyre tread bump at its intended depth (the texture is decoded to linear light, which made it about seven times shallower than drawn).Less: both headlamp lenses in one mesh and both tail lamps in another, two draws instead of four.
Race carCarbon fibre reflects less than paint: it gets the same reflection map at its own share of the strength.None: the same reflection map.
BoatAn even stamped-aluminium hull, and hull, seats, floor, cooler and tank as wood and plastic with only a little metal (they looked like bronze).None.
First-person hands and rodWarmer, pinker fingertips, worn leather lighter over the knuckles; a glossy painted rod blank, cork and wraps that are not metal, machined parts without tone variation.None: vertex colours and material values.
ParagliderThe sun shines through the fabric as through leaves; the closed cells are drawn one-sided.Less: the closed cells' hidden inside faces are no longer drawn.
White and red paint on buildings, the lighthouse and the pit stopPainted whites at a real paint's brightness (they burned out in full sun) and the reds a little deeper, so both keep their shading; ends that fought for the same pixels made a hair shorter.None.
Geyser, wreck and sea stacksThe geyser cone coloured ring by ring (an orange-brown foot where the runoff pools, grey-white sinter up the cone, a dark wet lip at the vent); the wreck rusted below the old waterline with black topsides, rust streaks and a white band along the rails, as rough paint, not metal; the sea stacks dark in the splash zone just above the sea and white with seabirds up to the grassy top.Less: the wreck shares the props' material instead of one of its own.
Calving glacierOld, dense ice deep blue low down and paler up, with a band of grit a third of the way up and a little variation face to face.None: vertex colours.
Tesla statue, coil house and scientists' bustsWeathered bronze (verdigris is not a metal: less metal, a little rougher); the coil house roof's shingle rows run along the eaves the right way up; the fine mesh fades to a see-through grey with distance instead of vanishing a few metres off.None: the mesh uses alpha to coverage on the multisampled frame, with no alpha test, instead of a hard cut.
Noise textures (clouds, rock, ground)Each octave's lattice shifted by its own fraction of a cell, so no faint square grid shows in clouds and rock, and blended with a curve whose slope is smooth across cell edges, so bump lighting has no creases. Clouds drawn out into wisps and streaks.Load time only; every texture the same size as before.
Gravel roadsPebbles in two sizes drawn round on the road (the texture is stretched along the road, so they are drawn taller than wide), each with a faint darker halo, and faint puddle stains and potholes; each road starts the texture at its own place.Load time only; the same texture size.
Planks, boards and panels (the finish texture)Joint lines with their edges eased over a texel, where a hard edge drew jagged lines that crawled as the camera moved.Load time only.
Particles (dust, spray, smoke)A soft round sprite, round in the middle and fading out softly at the rim, instead of a point in the middle and a hard rim.Load time only.
Ground near the cameraGravel stones vary warm to cool with a smooth step (a ringed pattern shimmered as the texture detail level changed).None.
Light and shade (all quality levels)The tone curve is Khronos PBR Neutral with three quarters of its black offset: the full offset, meant for glossy materials, crushed the shade of matte ground and plants to muddy black; with half of it the greens lost a tenth of their colour. Reflected sky light in the shade a little lower, so the sun gives the contrast. Under a grey sky the light is soft and nearly shadowless, the switch from the Sun to the Moon happens in the near darkness after sunset instead of in one jump, and moonlight turns toward where the sky draws the Moon as its light grows, so its shadows and its path on the lakes line up with it without swinging round at once.None: the same number of instructions as Neutral; only constants and light values changed.
Reflections on paint, chrome and glassThe reflection map is made again when the cloud cover has changed by a quarter, as well as every 4 degrees of the sun, so shade and reflections turn grey under a grey sky.A small cost at times: at most four more refreshes of a 128-pixel sky cube while the sky goes from clear to grey, at least 5 seconds apart.
ShadowsThe offset that stops surfaces shadowing themselves is now as small as each shadow map's texel allows: shadows were shortened and stones and logs had lost theirs altogether.None.
Distance and skyA little haze already in the middle distance (6% at 500 m and 13% at a kilometre, where it was 2% and 7%), fading toward the colour of the sky right behind each ridge, from the horizon colour low down to the zenith colour higher up; below the horizon the sky's stand-in for the land, which only reflections see, is olive instead of blue-grey.Less: the sky colour is worked out once per pixel instead of twice; the sky is drawn after everything solid, so its shader runs only where sky is seen.
Clouds and steamThin cloud edges let the light through and thick cores go grey underneath; steam and peak clouds get a silver lining when the sun is behind them.A few instructions per cloud pixel; the backlight is worked out once per puff on the processor.
WaterSun glints weighted like the reflection: faint looking straight down, strong across the water toward a low sun. White water at the falls and rapids is lit by the light the water itself gets, so it is dim at night and in a dark gorge instead of glowing.Less: the sky colour is worked out once instead of twice.
GrassWith the sun low behind them, the blade tips glow yellow-green, lit through.A few instructions per grass vertex.
Final picture (High)The gentle S-curve for depth applied to display values, where its pivot is a mid grey to the eye (in linear light it darkened the middle tones), and the grade's touch more colour raised from a tenth to three twentieths. Bloom only from real lights (the sun, glints, lamps, windows), not from sunlit snow and white clouds, which only softened the mountains. A cheaper, steadier noise against banding in the sky.Less: the noise is a multiply and two fractions instead of a sine.
Sky and water on Medium and LowThe same fine noise against banding where colour goes straight to the 8-bit screen.A few instructions per sky and water pixel.

sections.html:

Each number is the mean of three runs of the build. Between runs of the same build the still world at one place moved by up to 21 calls, so a difference of that size between the builds at one place is within the noise; the total over the eight places is steadier.

Memory and shaders

MeasureBeforeAfterChange
Textures the materials use8687+1
Their memory with mipmaps, MB104.77106.27+1.50
Textures the renderer holds1111110

The one more texture the materials use, 1.50 MB, is the scene's own reflection map: the race car's carbon now holds it as well, at its own share of the strength, so it reflects less than paint. It is no new memory: the textures the renderer holds are 111 before and 111 after (a 384 by 512 map in half floats is exactly 1.50 MB).

Work per pixel

Read in the shaders, since the test machine draws in software. Less: the sky is drawn after everything solid, so its shader runs only where sky is seen; the haze works out the sky colour once per pixel instead of twice, in every shader that has it; the final picture's noise against banding is a multiply and two fractions instead of a sine; the paraglider's closed cells no longer draw their hidden inside faces. A little more: a few instructions in the grass vertex shader (light through the tips), in the steam puffs (the silver lining), in the near trees' vertex shader (bark colour), and the fine noise on the sky and water on Medium and Low.

sections.title: What the audit found, and what was fixed
sections.html:
Every shader built, without an error

A development build checks each shader program as it is first used (the release build skips the check to load faster). Both builds were loaded, everything in the world and the hands was compiled and drawn once at High, Medium and Low in turn, and frames were drawn at morning, sunset, night and in rain: 261 programs before with 0 failing, 254 after with 0 failing; the browser printed 1 and 1 errors or warnings, the same one each time: that the software renderer cannot compile shaders in parallel.

Regression scenarios on the final build

ScenarioWhat it coversPicturesResult

Clean: the scenario ran to its end with no page error, failed step, failed picture or error printed by the page.

The independent code review

A separate review of the whole change, told the definition of load above, looked for shader errors under every combination of settings, values that could turn into not-a-number, any added draw call, mesh, material, shader, texture or allocation, and visual and logic mistakes. It verified each finding against the code before reporting it.

FindingSeverityWhat was done
The rowboat's inside was lit from the wrong side. Its inner hull is a mirrored sphere; as a round part it now kept its own normals, which a mirror leaves pointing out while the faces turn in.High: visible at every dockFixed in the model builder: a mirrored part that keeps its normals has them turned to agree with its faces. Checked in Node: 126 of 126 triangles agree, where none did.
The Tesla coil cage turned into a solid drum from about 25 to 50 m: with an alpha test as well as alpha to coverage, three sharpens the alpha about the test value, and the far mipmap levels average about 0.3, above the 0.15 test.Medium: visibleFixed: alpha to coverage alone, with no alpha test, so the mesh fades to a see-through grey with distance as intended.
About four more shader programs than before, and one more texture held from the start: a far-tree material with the bark rule and its reflection copy (two), a fish body shader without the sheen in the world and in the hands (two), a shadow shader for alpha-to-coverage fins (one), less the snag shader removed; and the pike probes that compiled the new fish shader uploaded a 512 by 256 skin.Medium: loadFixed: the far broadleaf trees share the far-foliage shader again; fish without the sheen keep a faint trace of it (0.02), so every fish shares one body shader, and the pike probes are gone; fins cast no shadow. Measured afterwards in the budget below.
The tops of some sea stacks lost the seabirds' white: the grass cone was skipped by height, which also skipped rock poking out above its foot (25 to 53 rock vertices on 3 of 5 stacks sampled).Medium to low: visibleFixed: the grass is told apart by its colour instead.
The sea stacks' wet band was measured from their base on the sea floor, 4 to 9 m under the surface, so it was never seen.Low: visibleFixed: measured from the sea's surface.
The darkening at the foot of static models also darkened faces turned up to the open sky: about 16% on a table top, 23 to 28% on decks and porches, about 31% on anything lying on the ground.Low: visibleFixed: faces turned up to the sky are left out; sides and undersides keep it.
A flat rock slab under water still stopped the boat as if it were a full-height boulder: its collider kept the old height.Low: playFixed: the collider's top follows the slab's height.
Night shadows swung round at moonrise and moonset: the light jumped from the stand-in direction to the real Moon in one step.Low: visibleFixed: the light turns toward the Moon as its light grows.
An array was made every frame while the sky was overcast.Low: memory churnFixed: made once.
The reflection map was refreshed whenever the cloud cover changed by a tenth: about eight more refreshes a minute while the weather changed.Low: load at timesReduced: a quarter, so at most four refreshes over a whole change from clear to grey, at least 5 seconds apart. Listed as a cost below.
The mist colour function was no longer called; its formula had been copied into two places.Low: codeFixed: one function, given the sky colour already worked out.
The bark colour shader chunk left out three's branches for colours with alpha and for batched meshes, so it would not compile with them (no current model uses either).Low: latentFixed: all of three's branches kept.

What the pictures and the tests themselves showed

FoundWhat was done
The first after picture of the forest was far darker than its before: a cloud's shadow lay over it. Cloud shadows drift with the game's clock, which runs at a different pace in each run, and this round changed the cloud pattern itself.The fixed views now hold cloud shadows at zero for both builds, and say so in their log.
The black bear view never had a bear in it, before or after: black bears live in the bear system, not among the wildlife the view searched, and the Bear Falls view before it sends the roaming bears away.The view now looks in the bear system and brings a black bear back for its picture.
Draw-call counts at a place moved with whichever animals and fish happened to be in view (Bear Falls showed 10 more after, from bears and fish).The budget check now counts the still world apart from the animals, fish, insects and other things that move about at random.
With half of Neutral's black offset the fifteen views lost a tenth of their colour (mean saturation 0.50 to 0.45), which read as washed out.Three quarters of the offset, and the High grade's touch of colour at 1.15: the saturation is back (see the pictures' numbers below), with more detail kept in the shade.
Lakes looked very different between builds in some views (the glacier lake pale in one and dark teal in the other, the lake at night lit warm in one): the game renews one face of the water's reflection cube a frame and the sky's reflection map at most every 5 seconds, and at a software renderer's frame rate the pictures still held reflections from the view before. Taken fresh, the two builds' night reflections were the same (their cubes compared face by face).Each fixed view now makes both reflections afresh for its place and hour before its picture. The reflection probe's stand-in for the water round it also keeps the plain horizon colour it had before the sky gradient.

sections.title: What this report cannot show
sections.html:
• No real iPhone or iPad was used. The pictures and the timings come from Chromium drawing in software on the test machine. The changes to colour, light and shading are the same on any device, but how a phone's graphics chip handles them was not measured.
  • The frame times are the processor's side of each frame. The tour skips the draw calls themselves, so work done per pixel on a graphics chip is not in these numbers. It was judged by reading the shaders instead (see Work per pixel).
  • The smallest difference the timings could see is about 0.57 ms a frame at 320 by 180 and 0.37 ms at an iPhone's size: the half-widths of the 95% intervals. A cost smaller than that could still be there.
  • Fifteen views, not every corner. The views cover the main kinds of place and light; the regression scenarios add close looks at most models. A fault in a place none of them looks at would not show here.
  • "Perceived quality" was judged by eye from the pairs, with the pictures' own numbers (brightness, contrast, colour) as a check that the after pictures are not simply darker, brighter, flatter or more washed out than the before.
  • Sources were read through web search. curl is blocked for every host in this environment, so the pages below were found and summarised by search, not downloaded in full. To allow hosts: the cloud environment menu in the session's title bar, then Edit, then Network access (a broader level, or Custom with the hosts added under Allowed domains); the steps are at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#network-access.

sections.title: What would change this conclusion
sections.html:
The conclusion: every family of assets looks better for the same work. The still world draws 1603.7 calls where it drew 1605.0 over the eight budget places, the shader programs went from 105 to 102, the renderer holds the same 111 textures and the frame time moved by +0.08 ms at 320 by 180 and +0.04 ms at an iPhone's size, neither of them a difference these runs can tell from zero. This conclusion would change if:

  • A phone's graphics chip finds the new per-pixel work heavier than reading the shaders suggests. The added work is a few instructions in the grass, the steam and the near trees, and fine noise on Medium and Low; the sky now runs only where sky is seen. The test that would settle it is the two builds taking turns on the same iPhone, timed with Safari's Web Inspector on the frame timeline.
  • A view the tests do not look at shows a fault. The rowboat's inside and the coil cage were found by the review, not by the pictures. A face of a model mirrored and kept round, or a far mipmap level of a see-through texture, would be the first places to look.
  • Players prefer the old colour. The tone curve keeps three quarters of Neutral's black offset: more detail in the shade, the same colourfulness on average. If the shade looks too light on a phone's screen in daylight, the offset can go back toward the full 0.04 in one constant.
  • The weather changes far more often than it does now. The reflection map is made again at most four more times over a whole change from clear to grey; with weather changing every few seconds that would add up.
